features.text: The patient is 27 years old and female.
The patient has been experiencing right knee pain for a few weeks.
The knee pain is worse during breaststroke swimming.
The knee pain is described as a dull ache that becomes sharper with specific movements.
The pain occurs only during swimming and not constantly.
The patient has not noticed any swelling, instability, or stiffness in the knee.
The sharp pain occurs when kicking legs out like a frog during the breaststroke.
The pain worsens with continued swimming and started after increased swimming activity.
The patient has not had any prior issues with the knee before increased swimming.
The patient had an X-ray of the knee, which was normal.
The X-ray showed no swelling but pain upon patellar movement and leg stiffening.
The patient was diagnosed with chondromalacia of the patella by the doctor.
The pain is located on the front of the right knee, around the patella area.
The pain does not radiate to other areas.
The patient has not noticed any clicking, popping, or grinding sensations in the knee.
The patient has not noticed any weakness in the quadriceps or difficulty with straight leg raises.
The patient has no history of patellar dislocation or subluxation.
The knee pain is only caused by breaststroke swimming and not by other activities.
The pain has not improved with rest and the patient has not tried specific exercises yet.
The patient has not had an MRI or other advanced imaging of the right knee.
The patient has not noticed any locking, catching, or giving way of the knee.
The patient has not experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in the right leg.
The patient has not changed swimming technique or increased training intensity recently.
The patient has not noticed any specific movements or positions outside of swimming that reproduce the knee pain.
The patient has not experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in the distribution of the femoral or peroneal nerves.
The patient does not have the results of an MRI yet.
